sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-4: Use argument based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to support an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors and specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively

legend.name: Stored food
legend.meaning: The cotyledon is packed with food

legend.name: Leaves
legend.meaning: Green, so they can make food from sunlight

steps.title: Seed coat
steps.instruction: Trace the seed coat around the opened bean.

note.text: A seed is a baby plant packed with food inside a tough coat. The coat protects it until it sprouts.

steps.title: Cotyledon
steps.instruction: Trace the big half that fills the seed.

note.text: A bean splits into two halves, the cotyledons, or seed leaves. They're packed with stored food.

steps.title: Radicle
steps.instruction: Trace the tiny root tip of the embryo.

note.text: The embryo is the baby plant. Its radicle, the embryonic root, grows into the plant's first root.
The plumule holds the first young leaves and the shoot tip.

steps.title: Soil
steps.instruction: Draw the soil line for the seedling.

note.text: When a seed gets water and warmth, it sprouts. This is germination.
The radicle comes out first and grows down into a root that takes in water.
In a bean, the stem below the seed leaves grows and lifts them up out of the soil.

steps.title: Seed leaves
steps.instruction: Trace the two cotyledons on the stem.

note.text: The seedling lives on the food in the cotyledons until its first leaves can make food.

steps.title: First leaves
steps.instruction: Trace the first leaves at the top.

note.text: The plumule grows into the first true leaves, which make food by photosynthesis.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the stored food tan and the leaves green.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Seed coat: The seed coat is the thin outer layer. This big food store is a cotyledon.

mistakes.Radicle: The radicle becomes the root. These tiny leaves are the plumule.

steps.title: Food before leaves
steps.question: A seed sprouts underground in the dark. Where does it get food to grow?

options.text: From the food stored in its cotyledons
options.feedback: Yes. The stored food lasts until the first leaves reach light and start photosynthesis.

options.text: From sunlight through the seed coat
options.feedback: It's dark underground. The seedling uses food stored in the cotyledons.
Roots take in water and minerals, but the food comes from the cotyledons.
The seed has left the parent plant. Its food is packed in the cotyledons.

steps.title: Argue
steps.question: How does the seed coat help a plant reproduce?

options.text: It protects the embryo, so it survives until conditions are right to sprout
options.feedback: Right. A protected seed can wait out cold or drought, so its chance of growing into a plant goes up.
The food is stored in the cotyledons. The coat protects the embryo.
The radicle becomes the root. The coat protects the embryo.
Petals attract bees. The seed coat protects the embryo inside.
